author: Diptanu Choudhury
text: We are seeing backlash against sandboxes for primarily a couple of reasons - vendors don't support users to overcommit compute. You can't pay for N cores and overcommit the number of sandboxes that are run on those cores. In reality agents don't uniformly use resources during [quoting @arlanr: 'Turning the entire web into a filesystem. Code hallucinations are not a model problem. They're a data problem. Every day, APIs ship breaking changes, deprecate endpoints, and rename parameters.']
suggestedEngagement: Affirm the overcommit point from a scheduling angle — ask if they're considering work-stealing or bursty reservation models like Nomad's
Challenge or probe the data problem framing: ask whether dynamic API fetching at inference time is viable or if there's a better approach for agent tooling
Share perspective on sandbox adoption blockers from a consultancy angle: pricing models vs. technical trust, which is the bigger blocker?

author: Matt Mazur
text: The "Assessing Claude Mythos Preview's cybersecurity capabilities" post has me saying "wtf" over and over and over again. Like, holy crap: > During our testing, we found that Mythos Preview is capable of identifying and then exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in every major OS and web browser...

author: Ashish Rajan
text: 🚨 Hot take: AI won't fail because of models. It'll fail because of everything around them. After years as a CISO and now deep in AI security, I keep seeing the same gaps across orgs. So here's the simple framework teams I work with are using 👇 • Inventory AI tools • Define...

author: Tal Raviv
text: A year ago, "agent harness" was tools in a loop. In 2026, AI agent harness companies (Claude, Cursor, Codex, etc) are competing on: • How you can call your agent (local computer, mobile remote, messaging apps, tag in slack) • How it calls itself automatically (heartbeats, schedules)...
suggestedEngagement: Add a dimension to the competition: 'One missing axis: how the harness handles security policy at runtime — the companies that crack policy enforcement at the harness level will win enterprise'
Ask whether he sees harnesses converging to a standard (like browsers did) or remaining fragmented by use case
Share the consultancy lens: 'Working with enterprise clients, harness choice is now the most consequential technical decision — often more than model selection. Are you seeing that too?'
